headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from shared document-to-LLM workflows; plano’s broad egress makes downstream misuse more consequential.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: PaddleOCR ingests documents/images and can run browsers, while plano accepts API-driven LLM traffic and config files. If PaddleOCR output is passed into plano without sanitization, attacker-controlled document text can become instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance or isolation, so the interaction is plausible in default document-processing pipelines.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is forwarded into plano prompts or tool instructions without filtering, injection is possible.
IF the operator uses a shared workspace or copy-paste bridge between the two agents, attacker text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Add a strict content-delimiting wrapper around OCR text.
Strip or escape instruction-like tokens before sending text to plano.
Require human review for any prompt assembled from OCR output.
Use separate workspaces for OCR artifacts and LLM prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags from OCR to downstream prompts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images, and plano handles logs, traces, and metrics with broad network egress. If document contents or OCR artifacts are routed through plano, sensitive material can leak into telemetry or outbound API calls. The profiles do not show shared storage, but the default API-based workflow makes leakage plausible.
conditions: IF documents or OCR outputs are included in plano prompts, logs, or traces, leakage occurs.
IF plano is configured to retain request payloads, sensitive document text may persist outside the OCR system.
mitigations: Disable payload logging in plano.
Redact OCR text before sending it to any API.
Keep document artifacts in a separate directory from gateway logs.
Review outbound destinations for any OCR-derived content.
requires-engineering: enforce field-level data-loss prevention on prompt construction.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: PaddleOCR has allowlisted egress and browser execution, while plano has broad egress but no browser or subprocess spawning and does not support multiple instances. Their write surfaces do not overlap in the profiles, so direct resource contention is limited. Any conflict would require an external orchestrator or shared mutable state not shown here.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external resource through an orchestrator, contention can occur.
IF the operator shares a single config or output directory between them, file-level conflicts may appear.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Avoid sharing mutable API credentials between the agents.
Serialize any writes through a single orchestrator.
Check for accidental config overlap before deployment.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared external resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR produces extracted text from documents, and plano is an LLM gateway that can route or forward that text to downstream models or APIs. If plano treats OCR output as authoritative without verification, OCR mistakes or prompt-shaped text can cascade into incorrect actions or responses. The pairwise pathway is inferred from documented roles, not directly observed.
conditions: IF plano forwards OCR text into downstream model calls without validation, errors can cascade.
IF downstream consumers act on plano outputs as facts, OCR hallucinations or misreads can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before forwarding OCR text.
Require confidence thresholds for OCR-derived fields.
Mark OCR output as untrusted in downstream prompts.
Sample-check a few extracted records before automation.
requires-engineering: add structured validation against source documents.

E_compliance.rationale: PaddleOCR processes documents and images, while plano stores logs, traces, and metrics and uses broad egress. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a limited compliance concern exists: if regulated document data is routed through plano telemetry, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not show PHI or EU-only handling, so higher severity is not justified.
conditions: IF regulated document data is sent into plano logs or traces, retention policy mismatch can arise.
IF the deployment handles EU PII or PHI, the current profiles do not show matching controls.
mitigations: Disable verbose logging for document payloads.
Classify document data before routing it through plano.
Keep regulated data out of telemetry fields.
Review retention settings on both systems.
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing and retention controls.
